description: Snowflake type-checks PREDICATE POSITION at compile time: a bare column whose static type is VARCHAR or NUMBER is rejected with 'Invalid data type [VARCHAR(16777216)] for predicate [IS_DIRECT]' - the predicate itself is never implicitly TO_BOOLEAN'ed. Operands nested under a boolean operator (AND / NOT) still coerce through TO_BOOLEAN's text forms - 'true'/'t'/'yes'/'y'/'on'/'1', case-insensitive, and numbers as zero / non-zero - and the portable idioms are an explicit comparison or an explicit TO_BOOLEAN call. The fixture's UNION ALL takes its column type from the FIRST branch, a BOOLEAN literal, so every later branch's string is converted by TO_BOOLEAN before it reaches the VARCHAR column and 'Y' lands as 'true'; live-verified, the stored flags are true/false/true/false/true, so both explicit forms select ids 1, 3 and 5. Converted 1:1 from query/BooleanCoercionInPredicateTest (now retired); the Java counted rows, and the converted tests state WHICH rows so a coercion that selected the wrong three would fail.

SELECT id FROM t WHERE is_direct
